heroHeadline: Russian Drone Strike Kills Infant in Marhanets as Ukraine Hits Ust-Luga Oil Port for Sixth Time
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,633, a Russian nighttime drone strike on a Marhanets high-rise killed a three-month-old infant and injured 11, part of a 152-drone overnight barrage that also hit Zaporizhzhia and Odesa Oblast; it followed an Aug 14 double-drone strike on a home in Buryn, Sumy Oblast that killed a mother and her 9-year-old son. Ukraine continued its energy-infrastructure campaign, striking Russia's Ust-Luga Baltic oil port for the sixth time in 2026 and damaging processing units at the Novatek gas complex, while Russian guided bombs killed two and injured 17 in Kramatorsk. The UN's human rights monitoring mission raised its confirmed Ukrainian civilian death toll to 16,874 (incl. 820 children) with 51,273 wounded since Feb 24, 2022 — after July 2026 was recorded as the deadliest month for civilians since the war's opening weeks. Russian military losses reached ~1,464,440 since 2022 per the Ukrainian General Staff, as the US House began advancing the Senate-passed Lindsey Graham Russia sanctions act, though a floor vote is not expected before September.
footerNote: Data sourced from official government reports, UN monitoring missions, major international outlets, and institutional analyses. Historical data draws on peer-reviewed scholarship. Casualty figures are contested; ranges reflect scholarly and official estimates.
